text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific nature of your chronic bladder discomfort and how frequently you are urinating. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any blood in your urine, pain during urination, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of frequency, urgency, nocturia, and pain relieved by voiding, combined with recent dyspareunia, are highly suggestive of a lower urinary tract issue. Given your age and the nature of the pain during intercourse, could you describe the character of the bladder pain (e.g., suprapubic tenderness) and have you experienced any spotting or abnormal discharge? speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results showing a post-void residual of 25 mL are normal and rule out urinary retention, but the persistent symptoms despite normal imaging suggest a non-infectious inflammatory process. Given your history of pain with intercourse and relief of discomfort after voiding, have you noticed any thick, stringy discharge from the urethra or any changes in vaginal discharge?
